sort_pyfile.py.summary: Reorder the top-level statements of a Python script.
details: Parses the module with :mod:`ast`, sorts its top-level statements (imports and definitions included) and rewrites the file while keeping the original source segments.
sort_pyfile.py.notes: Reordering top-level statements can break a script whose body depends on its order.

sort_quotes.py.summary: Deduplicate a quotes JSON file and sort it by author.
details: Loads the list of ``{"quote", "author"}`` objects, drops the duplicate quotes (compared case-insensitively) and writes the list back sorted by author.

sortbylen.py.summary: Sort the lines of a file by their length.
details: Reads the file keeping the line endings, sorts the lines by length (``-r`` for the longest first) and writes them back in place.

sortbysize.py.summary: Write a JSON list of the current directory's entries sorted by total size.
details: Measures each file and each directory (recursively, symlinks excluded) of the current directory and saves the descending ``[{"name", "size"}]`` list to ``<directory-name>.json``.

sorted_pkgs.py.summary: List the installed packages by size in a table.
details: Queries dpkg for the installed packages, caches the result in ``installed.json`` (``-r`` refreshes it) and prints a width-adaptive table with human-readable sizes, optionally filtered to the biggest ones.

soverify.py.summary: Verify that the shared objects below the current directory actually load.
details: Loads each ``.so`` file with ctypes, reports the failures and writes a JSON report to ``/sdcard/soverify.log``; a Python-API wrapper around the process keeps the interpreter stable while the libraries are probed.

spdf.py.summary: Shrink PDF files with Ghostscript's screen profile.
details: Runs ``gs`` with 85 dpi downsampling and font subsetting into a temporary file and replaces the original only when the result is smaller, printing the before/after sizes and the space saved. Files are processed in parallel.

spdf2.py.summary: Optimise PDF files with qpdf's object streams.
details: Runs ``qpdf --linearize --object-streams=generate`` into a temporary file and keeps it only when it is smaller than the original, reporting the sizes and the total space freed. Files are processed in parallel.

split_json.py.summary: Write every value of a JSON list of objects to its own text file.
details: Reads the list, skips the entries that are not objects and writes each key/value pair to a ``.txt`` file named after the key, adding an index suffix when the name is already taken.

split_movies_list.py.summary: Group a list of movie URLs into one text file per movie.
details: Reads the URLs from the given file, takes the name that follows ``/series/`` in each URL and writes the URLs of each movie to ``split_movies/<movie>.txt`` with a sanitised file name.

splitby.py.summary: Put every occurrence of a delimiter on its own line.
details: Splits the file on the delimiter, strips each part and rewrites the file with one part per line followed by the delimiter.

sqltojson.py.summary: Run SQL queries defined in YAML/JSON config files and export the results to JSON or CSV.
details: Reads the connection and query definitions (a config file or the ``queries`` folder), binds the parameters and the date placeholders (``CURRENT_DATE`` and the month/year boundaries), executes the statements in a read-only transaction with SQLAlchemy and writes the rows as JSON, NDJSON or CSV. The CLI is driven by ``fire``.

squizer.py.summary: Compress Python sources by renaming names, dropping docstrings and self-extracting the result.
details: Strips the docstrings and annotations, removes the unused stdlib imports, renames the local names to short ones, joins the simple statements and optionally emits a single self-decoding ``b85``/``zlib`` payload, keeping the builtins and the protected names untouched.

srpr.py.summary: Run ``srp`` once for every ASCII letter.
details: Calls the external ``srp`` command with each lowercase and then each uppercase letter, printing the output of each run.
srpr.py.notes: Wrapper around the external ``srp`` executable; it does nothing useful without it.
